stories.title: VA care linked to lower suicide rates in Army veterans
stories.summary: Army veterans who used Veterans Health Administration care after returning from Afghanistan or Iraq had a 20 percent lower suicide rate than those who did not, according to a research letter in JAMA Network Open. The study does not prove causation. Follow-up for the data ended in 2018.

stories.title: Mental disorders reported in 17.5 percent of Chinese youth
stories.summary: A nationwide study led by Beijing Anding Hospital found 17.5 percent of children and adolescents in China have mental disorders. Anxiety and depression were the most common conditions. Researchers noted the figure may be an underestimate because the sample excluded children who do not attend school.

stories.title: Study finds high depression symptoms among Bangladeshi students
stories.summary: Nearly 75 percent of university students in Bangladesh show symptoms of depression, according to a study presented at Jagannath University. The research surveyed 422 undergraduate and postgraduate students aged 18 to 26. Findings were unveiled in collaboration with the Bangladesh Youth Think Tank and the mental health organisation BONDHU.

stories.title: India faces shortage of forensic psychiatrists
stories.summary: India has fewer than 30 forensic psychiatrists for its 1.5 billion people, according to data presented at the International Forensic Psychiatry Conference. Australia, by comparison, has 900 forensic psychiatrists for less than 30 million people. Many Indian-trained psychiatrists currently practice in Australia and New Zealand.

stories.title: Mindfulness trial targets dementia risk in older adults
stories.summary: A virtual mindfulness program for older adults enrolled 60 participants who reported subjective cognitive decline and elevated dementia risk factors. The feasibility trial, published in BMC Geriatrics, saw 407 people inquire about the study. The program aims to address modifiable risk factors for Alzheimer’s disease.

stories.title: Intensive breathing exercises may mimic psychedelic effects
stories.summary: Intensive breathwork can induce psychedelic experiences, including vivid imagery and a sense of unity, by reducing brain blood flow by 45 percent. Researchers found that the depth of the altered state did not correlate with the drop in blood supply. The brain is apparently capable of tripping itself.

stories.title: Study links sleep apnea genes to metabolic traits
stories.summary: A multivariate genome-wide association study reveals that obstructive sleep apnea shares a common genetic liability with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and adiposity. Researchers integrated European-ancestry data to derive a latent factor representing the shared genetic architecture of these conditions. The disorders frequently co-occur for a reason.

stories.title: Researchers propose circadian depression subtype
stories.summary: A study of 11,380 Australian adults suggests a new depression subtype linked to circadian rhythms. About 23 percent of participants exhibited traits like evening chronotypes and seasonal mood shifts. The researchers term this circadian depression, though it remains a proposed profile rather than a formal clinical diagnosis.

stories.title: Sleep patterns may identify proposed depression profile
stories.summary: Researchers studying 11,380 Australian adults identified a proposed depression profile linked to sleep-wake patterns. About 23 percent of participants met criteria for circadian depression, defined by features like social jetlag and seasonal mood changes. The profile is not a formal diagnosis and requires independent replication.

stories.title: Sleep habits could signal hidden depression subtype
stories.summary: In a study of 11,380 Australian adults, 23 percent met criteria for a proposed depression subtype linked to internal clocks. Features include evening chronotypes, social jetlag, and seasonal variations in mood or appetite. The researchers call this circadian depression, though it is not yet a formal diagnosis.

stories.title: Writing to-do lists before bed may help sleep
stories.summary: A Baylor University study of 57 adults found that writing a to-do list before bed helps people fall asleep faster. Researchers suggest this five-minute task offloads mental burdens that otherwise keep the brain rehearsing tomorrow's agenda. The notepad is apparently more effective than the internal monologue.

stories.title: Sleep breathing issues linked to brain barrier markers
stories.summary: Researchers analyzed 409 participants to find an association between sleep-disordered breathing and blood-brain barrier dysfunction. Cerebrospinal fluid samples showed elevated biomarkers of compromised vascular integrity in those with respiratory disturbances. The study suggests a potential mechanistic link between sleep breathing and Alzheimer's disease pathology.

stories.title: Study identifies stress granule biomarkers in spinal cord injury
stories.summary: Researchers using RNA sequencing identified ARG1 and PLAUR as potential stress granule-related biomarkers in spinal cord injury. The analysis also highlighted monocytes and endothelial cells as key contributors to the condition. The specific functional roles of these stress granules in injury pathology remain under investigation.

stories.title: Older brains may adapt better to sleep loss
stories.summary: A Simon Fraser University study suggests healthy older brains may adapt to acute sleep loss differently than younger ones. After three hours of sleep, brain connections changed in opposite directions between the two groups. Healthy older brains appear to preserve function despite the lack of rest.

stories.title: Simple sleep metrics may outperform high-tech trackers
stories.summary: A study of 11 collegiate swimmers compared sleep monitoring devices to race times. The research suggests that the most effective metric for performance is far less sophisticated than the data provided by modern wearables. High-tech health metrics were not connected to better race results.

stories.title: Consistency may matter more than sleep duration
stories.summary: A 2024 study suggests that consistent bedtimes and wake times may be a stronger signal for long-term health than total hours logged. UC Berkeley scientist Matthew Walker notes this finding challenges the classic eight-hour rule. Regularity appears to be the primary factor for sleep health.

stories.title: Yoga-based rehab improves quality of life in heart failure
stories.summary: A study of 3,500 adults in India found that yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation improved quality of life and walking distance compared to standard care. However, there was no significant difference in the combined rate of death, hospitalization, or stroke. The program provided benefits beyond standard treatment.

stories.title: Strength training helps slow age-related muscle loss
stories.summary: Sarcopenia can begin affecting adults as early as age 30, with muscle mass decreasing by 3 to 8 percent per decade. Research suggests strength training is one of the most important ways to slow this decline. Maintaining upper-body strength supports independence in later life.

stories.title: Modified razor curl exercises improve hamstring strength
stories.summary: A six-week study of 45 male football players found that modified razor curl exercises improved eccentric hamstring strength and core endurance. The results suggest the protocol is a practical alternative to the nordic hamstring exercise. It may allow for a greater training volume during athlete interventions.

stories.title: Walking therapy offers mental health benefits
stories.summary: Walking therapy involves mindful nature walks with a mental health expert to treat conditions like anxiety and hypertension. Proponents suggest the practice combines physical exercise with meditation. The activity is currently gaining traction as a formal approach to improving mental and physical well-being.

stories.title: Hybrid training may improve longevity
stories.summary: An observational study of 147,000 health professionals suggests mortality risk is lowest among those who combine strength and cardio training. Combining one to two hours of resistance training with aerobic activity may add years to life. The practice flips the assumption that one must sacrifice the other.

stories.title: Walking offers accessible workout for midlife health
stories.summary: Walking is described as an effective, low-impact way to improve joint mobility, balance, and breathing. Coaches suggest the activity provides mental health benefits and serves as a complement to other exercise forms. It is presented as an accessible option for those looking to build fitness gradually.

stories.title: Vinyasa flow suggested for flexibility and strength
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Malaika Arora shares a beginner-friendly Vinyasa flow sequence intended to improve flexibility, build strength, and enhance balance. The routine is presented as an accessible entry point for those looking to incorporate yoga into their daily physical activity.

stories.title: Plant-based dairy swaps may lower nutrient intake
stories.summary: Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives can significantly reduce essential nutrient intake, according to a University of Surrey study. Substituting 20% to 35% of dairy increased the prevalence of inadequate iodine intake among adolescent girls from 54% to 65%. Fortification remains a suggested solution for the nutrient gap.

stories.title: Blueberry powder linked to mood improvement
stories.summary: Researchers in Boston found that daily consumption of blueberry powder for three months resulted in improved depressive symptoms in older adults. Depression is not a normal part of aging, though it is more common in those with existing health conditions. The study suggests a dietary boost for the blues.

stories.title: Experts advise gradual return to routine after festive feasting
stories.summary: Dieticians suggest that post-festive digestive discomfort is linked to larger portions and disrupted sleep. Experts advise a gradual return to balanced eating and regular activity rather than crash diets or long fasts. The body is expected to recover without the need for extreme reset measures.

stories.title: Kiwifruit study suggests digestive benefits
stories.summary: A review published in Food, Nutrition and Health suggests that two green kiwifruits daily may improve bowel movements and reduce discomfort in adults with chronic constipation. The narrative review examined potential benefits for functional constipation and constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome. Fruit is being tested for regularity.

stories.title: Toxicity archives may hold longevity clues
stories.summary: Researchers have identified chemical compounds that increased survival rates in rodent toxicity studies, suggesting existing safety archives could help find agents for healthy aging. Finding interventions that extend both lifespan and healthspan remains difficult. Preclinical research continues to look for shortcuts in the data.

stories.title: Kidney transplant study finds no longevity boost from rapamycin
stories.summary: A large evaluation of national organ transplant registry data found that long-term prescription of rapamycin did not yield meaningful improvement in patient longevity. The study compared thousands of kidney transplant recipients maintained on the drug against those on alternative regimens. The drug did not extend survival.

stories.title: Longevity study clarifies meat consumption findings
stories.summary: Recent headlines suggesting meat eaters live longer were based on a study of elderly populations. Researchers clarified the findings are not a recommendation for specific diets, but a warning about the risks of insufficient protein and calories in fragile, older bodies. The study was not about kale.

stories.title: Grip strength as a potential health marker
stories.summary: Research suggests that grip strength may offer clues about overall health and longevity, with weaker strength linked to higher risks of health problems. The ability to hold onto items has emerged as an unexpected marker of healthy aging. Experts are now suggesting next steps for those with weaker grips.

stories.title: VetCompass Study Unveils Health Demography and Lifespan of UK Shih Tzus
stories.summary: A comprehensive epidemiological investigation utilizing clinical records from the VetCompass Programme has characterized the demography, common disorder prevalence, and mortality patterns of Shih Tzu dogs receiving primary veterinary care across the United Kingdom. Drawing from an overall surveillance cohort of 336,865 dogs attending primary-care veterinary

stories.title: Ayurvedic institute construction remains stalled
stories.summary: Residents of two Haryana villages are waiting for work to begin on an Ayurvedic institute promised by Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini. The villagers previously ended a 320-day protest following the Chief Minister's assurance in May. The hospital has yet to appear on the promised panchayat land.

stories.title: Researchers propose reporting standards for Ayurvedic clinical trials
stories.summary: Researchers have proposed a methodological framework and eleven reporting extensions to adapt clinical trial protocols for Ayurvedic whole-system interventions. The proposal aims to integrate reproducibility and transparency into research. The authors designed these extensions for future Delphi consensus evaluation rather than for immediate clinical implementation in patients.

stories.title: Veterinary report details herbal treatment for refractory vomiting
stories.summary: A report from the Veterinary Teaching Hospital of Northwest A&F University describes three animals with chronic vomiting that resolved after receiving a modified Xuanfu Daizhe Decoction. Conventional treatments for such cases typically include antiemetics and acid suppression. The study notes the resolution of symptoms in the specific cases provided.

stories.summary: The Ministry of Ayush has reviewed the development of International Classification of Health Interventions and National Health Intervention Codes for Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani systems. The initiative aims to integrate traditional medicine into global frameworks under the World Health Organization. The coding system remains under development.

stories.title: All India Institute of Ayurveda reports ten years of patient data
stories.summary: The All India Institute of Ayurveda provided services to 3,774,524 patients between October 2016 and September 2026. The institute operates a 200-bed inpatient department and outpatient services with a daily capacity of 3,000 patients. The figures were released by the Ministry of Ayush to highlight clinical expansion.
